subject.title: [Feature]: Support running OpenClaw on devices without Linux / Node.js (inspired by MimiClaw)

question: Should OpenClaw define and support a runtime-neutral agent-core protocol for no-Node embedded or WASM ports, or should those ports remain external projects without a core compatibility contract?
rationale: Current source and docs show OpenClaw is still intentionally Node-hosted, and choosing a portable agent ABI affects core runtime ownership, plugin SDK boundaries, storage/session semantics, providers, tools, and security policy.

options.title: Keep as runtime-portability RFC
options.body: Use this issue to design the minimal schemas, conformance tests, and ownership boundary before accepting any embedded or WASM implementation.

options.title: Scope to plugin SDK work only
options.body: Route near-term language/runtime work through JSON-RPC/plugin-harness APIs and leave no-Node full runtime ports outside the supported OpenClaw contract.

options.title: Close as not planned
options.body: Decide that OpenClaw remains Node-hosted and external projects such as MimiClaw are independent ports without a compatibility promise.

recommendation.title: Keep as runtime-portability RFC
recommendation.body: Use this issue to design the minimal schemas, conformance tests, and ownership boundary before accepting any embedded or WASM implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant current history is around the runtime guard, harness registry, and recent agent-loop runtime work.
